difficultyReason: Transparent circular reasoning flaw. The stimulus concludes that vitamins help recovery because they contain recovery-promoting substances. This is circular: assuming the premise to reach the conclusion. Only one answer (D) replicates this exact self-supporting structure with different content. Other answers either contain valid reasoning or commit obviously different errors.
stimulus: All vitamins contain substances that promote recovery from illness. Vitamin C is a vitamin. Therefore, vitamin C promotes recovery from illness.
questionStem: Which one of the following exhibits flawed reasoning most similar to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All minerals are beneficial to health. Some beneficial substances are not minerals. Therefore, some beneficial substances might be minerals.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All cells contain DNA. Cancer is caused by mutated cells. Therefore, cancer is caused by mutated DNA.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All universities have professors. The University of Chicago is a university. Therefore, the University of Chicago has professors.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All honest people tell the truth. Jim tells the truth. Therefore, Jim is honest.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most birds can fly. Penguins are birds. Therefore, penguins can probably fly.

explanations.correct: The stimulus commits affirming the consequent: 'All X have property P → If something has P, is it X?' The conclusion assumes the inverse of the conditional. D does the same: 'All honest people tell the truth' does not imply that all truth-tellers are honest, but the argument assumes it does. Both are classical logical fallacies of conditional reversal.
explanations.A: Valid reasoning with proper quantifiers; no flaw.
explanations.B: Combines two premises to reach a valid intermediate conclusion; not a conditional reversal.
explanations.C: Valid application of a universal premise to a member of the category; this is sound reasoning.
explanations.D: Correct. Stimulus: All P are Q; X is Q; therefore X is P (affirming the consequent). D: All honest are truth-tellers; Jim is a truth-teller; therefore Jim is honest. Exact same flaw.
explanations.E: Different flaw — quantifier mismatch (probabilistic generalization to a specific case), not a conditional reversal.

difficultyReason: Transparent false dichotomy. The stimulus presents only two options (study hard or fail) and eliminates one, concluding the other must be true. This is transparent because the structure is immediately visible and no other answer replicates it. Trap answers introduce unrelated fallacies or valid reasoning.
stimulus: Either you study hard for the exam or you will fail. Since you did not study hard, you will definitely fail.
questionStem: Which one of the following arguments contains flawed reasoning most similar to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Either the defendant is guilty or innocent. The evidence shows the defendant acted with intent. Therefore, the defendant is guilty.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A restaurant is either expensive or cheap. Since this restaurant is not expensive, it must be cheap.

choices.label: C
choices.text: If you do not exercise regularly, you will gain weight. You exercise regularly. Therefore, you will not gain weight.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All successful companies innovate. This company is successful. Therefore, this company innovates.

choices.label: E
choices.text: People are either optimists or pessimists. Research shows most people are adaptable. Therefore, most people are neither optimists nor pessimists.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: False dilemma—assumes only two options (study hard OR fail), eliminates one, concludes the other. B: False dilemma—assumes only two options (expensive OR cheap), eliminates one, concludes the other. Identical structure and identical flaw.
explanations.A: Premises do not establish a dichotomy; the reasoning is invalid for different reasons.
explanations.B: Correct. Both stimulus and B set up a false binary choice, eliminate one option, and conclude the remaining option must be true.
explanations.C: This is a conditional premise with a negated antecedent; not a false dichotomy.
explanations.D: Valid categorical reasoning; no flaw of false dichotomy.
explanations.E: Introduces a contradiction but doesn't use the dichotomy flaw in the way the stimulus does.

difficultyReason: Transparent ad hominem. The stimulus rejects a claim solely because of who made it (a competitor), not by engaging with the claim itself. Only one answer (C) commits the same ad hominem error. Other answers are valid arguments or commit different logical errors.
stimulus: The rival pharmaceutical company claims that our drug is ineffective. But the rival company has a financial incentive to discredit us. Therefore, our drug must be effective.
questionStem: Which one of the following arguments exhibits flawed reasoning most similar to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dr. Smith claims that the new vaccine is safe. Dr. Smith has conducted extensive research on vaccines. Therefore, the new vaccine is safe.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The defense attorney argues that the witness is unreliable. The witness has been convicted of perjury in the past. Therefore, the defense attorney's argument is valid.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The activist claims that the factory pollutes the environment. But the activist is known for exaggerating problems. Therefore, the factory does not pollute the environment.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The economist predicts a recession. The economist has never been accurate in the past. Therefore, there will be no recession.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The politician supports the tax increase. The politician is wealthy. Therefore, the tax increase is unjust.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: Ad hominem—rejects a claim (drug is ineffective) by attacking the source (rival has incentive to lie), then concludes the opposite of the claim. D: Ad hominem—rejects a claim (recession will occur) by attacking the source's character (never accurate), then concludes the opposite. Both assume that discrediting the source proves the claim false, which is the ad hominem flaw.
explanations.A: Appeals to the source's credibility; valid reasoning, not ad hominem.
explanations.B: Legitimately questions reliability; not the same ad hominem structure as stimulus.
explanations.C: Correct. Stimulus: Source has incentive to lie, therefore claim is false. C: Source exaggerates, therefore claim is false. Both reject a claim via ad hominem attack.
explanations.D: Correct. Stimulus: Rival is biased, so our drug works. D: Economist is inaccurate, so no recession. Both attack the messenger to refute the message.
explanations.E: Attacks the source's motives but doesn't conclude the claim is false; different structure.

difficultyReason: Transparent necessary/sufficient confusion. The stimulus treats a necessary condition as sufficient: if something is required for success, the stimulus assumes having it guarantees success. Only one answer (B) replicates this exact reversal. Other answers either use conditionals correctly or commit different errors.
stimulus: A college degree is necessary for a successful career in law. Therefore, anyone with a college degree will have a successful law career.
questionStem: Which one of the following exhibits flawed reasoning most similar to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Water is necessary for plant growth. Therefore, some plants cannot grow without water.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A valid passport is necessary for international travel. Therefore, anyone with a valid passport can travel internationally.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Practice is necessary for mastering an instrument. Therefore, you should practice every day.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sleep is necessary for health. Most healthy people sleep regularly. Therefore, most healthy people are well-rested.

choices.label: E
choices.text: A license is necessary to drive legally. Most licensed drivers follow traffic laws. Therefore, most drivers are licensed.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: Necessary condition stated (college degree is necessary for law success), then treated as sufficient (anyone with degree → success). B: Necessary condition stated (passport is necessary for international travel), then treated as sufficient (anyone with passport → can travel). Both confuse a requirement with a guarantee.
explanations.A: Correctly states a necessary condition without treating it as sufficient; valid reasoning.
explanations.B: Correct. Stimulus: College degree is necessary for law success, so having a degree guarantees success. B: Passport is necessary for travel, so having a passport guarantees ability to travel. Same flaw.
explanations.C: Normative claim, not a logical flaw of conditional confusion.
explanations.D: Introduces a separate premise about frequency; not a simple necessary/sufficient confusion.
explanations.E: Reverses the direction of the necessary condition; different structure.

difficultyReason: Transparent begging the question (circular reasoning). The stimulus asserts that the novel is well-written because it received critical praise, but critical praise is itself a measure of literary quality. The conclusion restates the premise. Only one answer (E) replicates this circularity. Other answers use premises and conclusions logically distinct from each other.
stimulus: This novel must be well-written because it has received critical acclaim from major literary magazines. After all, critical acclaim is a sign of literary excellence.
questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is flawed in the same way as the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: This restaurant must serve excellent food because the chef trained at a prestigious culinary school and uses only fresh ingredients.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The president's policy must be effective because it was voted on by Congress. Voting is how Congress passes laws.

choices.label: C
choices.text: This athlete must be talented because he won multiple championships. Championships are competitive events.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The movie must be entertaining because millions of people watched it. Large audiences indicate popularity.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The scientific theory must be true because experts accept it. Acceptance by experts is how we identify true theories.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: Novel is well-written (conclusion) because of critical acclaim (premise), and critical acclaim = literary excellence (which is what well-written means). The justification for the premise is simply a restatement of the conclusion. E: Theory is true (conclusion) because experts accept it (premise), and expert acceptance = identifying true theories (which is what truth means in this context). Both beg the question.
explanations.A: Provides distinct grounds (training, ingredients) for the conclusion; not circular.
explanations.B: Attempts a logical move but the second sentence doesn't truly justify the first; different type of flaw.
explanations.C: Championships are evidence of talent, but the argument doesn't assume championships = talent; valid structure.
explanations.D: Popularity is a distinct property from entertainment; not begging the question.
explanations.E: Correct. Stimulus: Well-written because of critical acclaim, and critical acclaim is a sign of literary excellence (begs the question). E: True because experts accept it, and expert acceptance is how we identify truth (begs the question). Identical flaw.

difficultyReason: Transparent equivocation. The stimulus uses 'state' in two different senses (a nation-state versus an emotional state) in a single argument, creating an invalid inference. Only one answer (C) replicates equivocation on a word with multiple meanings. Other answers either avoid equivocation or commit different errors.
stimulus: Countries with strong states are politically stable. Psychology shows that people with a strong state of mind are resilient. Therefore, psychology explains political stability.
questionStem: Which one of the following contains flawed reasoning most similar to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Banks offer interest on savings. Interest in history is common among scholars. Therefore, banks and scholars share similar motivations.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The right to free speech is protected by law. Some people have a right to remain silent. Therefore, silence is protected by law.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Newspapers have political authority in democracies. Some news reports have political authority. Therefore, democracies are influenced by news reports.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Trees absorb carbon dioxide. Some carbon dioxide affects the climate. Therefore, trees affect the climate.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Successful investments require patience. Patients in hospitals require medical care. Therefore, successful investments require medical care.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: Uses 'state' to mean both 'nation-state' (premise 1) and 'mental/emotional state' (premise 2), then conflates them to reach an invalid conclusion. A: Uses 'interest' to mean both 'financial interest' (banks) and 'intellectual interest' (scholars), then conflates them. Both equivocate on a word with multiple meanings.
explanations.A: Correct. 'Interest' means financial return in the first sentence and intellectual curiosity in the second; conflating them is equivocation, matching the stimulus's equivocation on 'state.'
explanations.B: Uses distinct homonyms ('right' as right to speak vs. right to silence) but in a way that doesn't create the same equivocal flaw.
explanations.C: Conflates 'political authority' of newspapers (institutional) with authority of news reports (content), but the logical structure differs from the stimulus.
explanations.D: Moves from 'trees absorb CO2' to 'CO2 affects climate' to 'trees affect climate'—a chain of valid premises, not equivocation.
explanations.E: Correct. This is a clear equivocation on 'require': patience (required for success) vs. medical care (required for patients). Matches stimulus's equivocation on 'state.'

difficultyReason: Transparent composition fallacy. The stimulus attributes a property of the parts (individual scientists are fallible) to the whole (the scientific community), reaching an invalid conclusion. Only one answer (D) replicates this part-to-whole error. Other answers either reason validly about wholes or commit different fallacies.
stimulus: Individual scientists are sometimes wrong in their reasoning. Therefore, the scientific consensus must be wrong.
questionStem: Which one of the following exhibits flawed reasoning most similar to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Each chess piece has limited mobility. Therefore, no meaningful chess strategy is possible.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Some economists disagree about tax policy. Therefore, economics as a field is not a valid discipline.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Every brick in the wall is small. Therefore, every wall is small.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Individual musicians in an orchestra are not perfect. Therefore, orchestral performances are not excellent.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some athletes are not intelligent. Therefore, athletic competition requires no intelligence.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: Individual parts (scientists) have a property (fallibility), so the whole (scientific consensus) must lack the opposite property (be wrong). D: Individual parts (musicians) have a property (imperfection), so the whole (orchestral performance) must lack the opposite property (be excellent). Both commit the composition fallacy.
explanations.A: Correctly infers a limitation of the whole from a property of parts, but the flaw is different from the stimulus.
explanations.B: Attributes disagreement of individuals to invalidity of the field; related but different structure.
explanations.C: Composition fallacy, but concludes something obviously true (small bricks → small wall), making it less transparent.
explanations.D: Correct. Stimulus: Individual scientists are fallible, so scientific consensus is wrong. D: Individual musicians are imperfect, so orchestral performances are not excellent. Both wrongly infer that a property of parts determines the opposite property of the whole.
explanations.E: Commits an unsupported generalization; different flaw.

difficultyReason: Transparent division fallacy (inverse of composition). The stimulus attributes a property of the whole (the team is successful) to each part (every player is successful), reaching an invalid conclusion. Only one answer (E) replicates this whole-to-part error. Other answers reason validly or commit different fallacies.
stimulus: The basketball team won the championship. Therefore, every player on the team must be an excellent basketball player.
questionStem: Which one of the following arguments contains flawed reasoning most similar to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: This company is profitable. Therefore, the company must have a large number of employees.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The orchestra performed beautifully. Therefore, every instrument in the orchestra sounded beautiful.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The novel is long. Therefore, every chapter in the novel is long.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The committee is efficient. Therefore, the committee has efficient decision-making procedures.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The board of directors made a profitable investment. Therefore, each director individually made a profitable investment.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: Whole property (team won championship) → Individual part property (every player is excellent). B: Whole property (orchestra performed beautifully) → Individual part property (every instrument sounded beautiful). Both commit division fallacy by attributing the whole's property to all of its parts.
explanations.A: Attributes a property to the whole that doesn't necessarily follow from profitability; different flaw.
explanations.B: Correct. Stimulus: Team's success → each player's excellence. B: Orchestra's beauty → each instrument's beauty. Both wrongly infer that a property of the whole applies to each part.
explanations.C: Attributes the whole's length to parts; division fallacy, but less transparent because the conclusion is absurd.
explanations.D: Infers a method or structure from a property; different type of inference.
explanations.E: Correct. Stimulus: Team's championship → each player's excellence. E: Board's profitable investment → each director's profitable investment. Both wrongly distribute a collective achievement to individuals.

difficultyReason: Transparent false cause. The stimulus confuses temporal sequence (A happens before B) with causal relation (A causes B), reaching an invalid conclusion. Only one answer (C) replicates this post hoc ergo propter hoc fallacy. Other answers either reason validly about causation or commit different errors.
stimulus: The company implemented new management practices in January. The company's profits increased in February. Therefore, the new management practices caused the increase in profits.
questionStem: Which one of the following exhibits flawed reasoning most similar to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The government raised interest rates on Tuesday. The stock market declined on Thursday. Therefore, higher interest rates caused the stock market to decline.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A medication was prescribed in the morning. The patient felt better in the afternoon. Therefore, the medication was effective.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The city installed new traffic lights in March. Traffic accidents decreased in April. Therefore, the new traffic lights reduced traffic accidents.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The school hired new teachers in September. Student test scores improved in October. Therefore, the new teachers caused the improvement.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Interest rates are rising. Unemployment is also rising. Therefore, rising interest rates cause unemployment to rise.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: Post hoc ergo propter hoc—event A happens, then event B happens, so A caused B. No control for other factors. A: Interest rates raised (A), market declined (B), therefore A caused B. C and D are similar, but A is the most transparent because the temporal gap and alternate explanations are most obvious.
explanations.A: Correct. Stimulus: Management change → profit increase (assumes causation from sequence). A: Interest rate increase → market decline (assumes causation from sequence). Both commit post hoc ergo propter hoc.
explanations.B: Temporal sequence with a plausible causal link; not the same flaw as stimulus.
explanations.C: Correct. Stimulus: New practices → profit increase. C: New traffic lights → accident decrease. Both post hoc ergo propter hoc.
explanations.D: Correct. Stimulus: New management → profit increase. D: New teachers → test score improvement. Both post hoc ergo propter hoc.
explanations.E: Correlation without causation, but lacks the temporal sequence element that makes post hoc fallacy transparent.
